fields.statement: Built rhiza at the branch head (go build -trimpath) and ran it by hand in a scratch root/repo with RHIZA_* unset. rhiza run start --foreground on a command-step workflow: the step saw GOTMPDIR=<repo>/.git/rhiza/runs/<run id>/gotmp, the folder existed when the step ran (ls -ld), and a real `go build -x` inside the step reported WORK=<that gotmp>/go-build303976419, so go's $WORK sat outside the shared TMPDIR. After the run succeeded, and after a second run failed, runs/ held only the .jsonl journals with no <run id>/ folder left. A third run whose step ran kill -9 $PPID (rhiza died, exit 137) left runs/<id>/gotmp behind; rhiza run ls listed it as a run of its journal, not of the folder; rhiza run abandon <id> exited 0 and the <id>/ folder was gone. Agent steps (session_run GOTMPDIR) were not run by hand, since that would start real agents; they are covered only by the unit tests. go test -trimpath ./internal/run -run GoTmp|TmpDir: ok.

With the built binary in a scratch repo: a command step that printed 'could not import io (open $WORK/b033/_pkg_.a: no such file or directory)' and exited 1 on its first try only was rerun once. stderr showed one line, 'rhiza: step failed as go's $WORK folder vanished; running it once more', then second-ok, and the step passed (exit 0). A step that printed "can't create $WORK/b094/_pkg_.a: open $WORK/b094/_pkg_.a: no such file or directory" every time ran exactly twice, and the second failure stood (run failed, step detail exit 1). A step that failed with 'main.go:3: undefined: foo' ran once (counter file = 1) and was not rerun. go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run VanishedGoWork|GoWork|AbandonGoTmp|GoTmp|SessionRun printed PASS; rootguard then flagged an unrelated write to ~/code/.rhiza-root/usage.live.json.
